'''Christopher Tadeusz Czeslaw Sachrajda''' {{post-nominals|size=100%|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 15 November 1949) is a [[Great Britain|British]] physicist. He is a professor of physics at the [[University of Southampton]] since 1990.<ref name="whoswho" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hep.phys.soton.ac.uk/content/christopher-t-sachrajda|title=Christopher T. Sachrajda &#124; www.hep.phys.soton.ac.uk|access-date=20 March 2016|archive-date=31 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331191851/http://www.hep.phys.soton.ac.uk/content/christopher-t-sachrajda|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Education ==
Sachrajda earned his doctorate from [[Imperial College London]] in 1974.<ref name="whoswho" /> His thesis was entitled ''Applications of perturbation theory to the high energy scattering of elementary particles.''

== Research ==
Sachrajda has made contributions to the development of [[quantum chromodynamics]] (QCD), the theory of the [[strong interaction]]s. His work on the factorisation of mass singularities led to the [[perturbative]] prediction of many physical quantities in strong interaction physics. With others, he pioneered the calculation of higher-order corrections to deep inelastic [[structure function]]s, which has led to detailed tests of QCD and the determination of the [[momentum]] [[Distribution function (physics)|distribution]] of [[quark]]s and [[gluon]]s inside the [[proton]]. He has played a leading role in the development of the [[lattice QCD|lattice formulation of QCD]] into a quantitative [[non-perturbative]] technique and in the use of this formulation to compute, from first principles, a number of physical quantities, including deep inelastic structure functions, electromagnetic [[Electric form factor|form factor]]s of [[hadron]]s and semi-[[lepton]]ic [[Particle decay|decays]] of [[charm (quantum number)|charm]]ed [[meson]]s.<ref name="FRS" />

== Awards and honours ==
Sachrajda was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1996|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1996]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/christopher-sachrajda-12217|title=Christopher Sachrajda|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Licence]]." {{Cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=20 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220093712/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=20 February 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref><ref name="frsCitation">{{cite web|url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%27EC%2F1996%2F31%27%29|title=EC/1996/31: Sachrajda, Christopher Tadeusz Czeslaw|publisher=[[The Royal Society]]|accessdate=20 March 2016}}{{Dead link|date=October 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
